lem-continuous-riemann-lebesgue-agreemen:
## Statement

Assume Countable Choice. Let $g:[0,1]\to\mathbb R$ be continuous. Its Riemann integral and its Lebesgue integral with respect to Lebesgue measure on $[0,1]$ both exist and are equal.
lem-unit-interval-lebesgue-gauss-data-va:
## Statement

Assume Countable Choice. For every integer $M\ge1$, Lebesgue measure on the relative Borel space $[0,1]$ is Gaussian quadrature moment data of order $2M$ in the sense of [[def-gauss-moment-data]].
def-collocation-quadrature-tableau:
## Definition

Let $M,d\ge1$, let $0\le c_1<\cdots<c_M\le1$ be distinct collocation nodes, and let $\ell_1,\ldots,\ell_M$ be their cardinal polynomials from [[def-cardinal-polynomial-interpolation]]. Define
$$Q_{ij}:=\int_0^{c_i}\ell_j(s)\,ds,\qquad b_j:=\int_0^1\ell_j(s)\,ds.$$
The matrix $Q\in\mathbb R^{M\times M}$ and vector $b\in\mathbb R^M$ are the collocation tableau coefficients. For an IVP $y'=f(t,y)$ on the open domain of [[def-first-order-ode-initial-value-problem-and-solution]], write
$$F_j(U):=f(t+c_jh,U_j),\qquad QF(U):=\left(\sum_{j=1}^M Q_{ij}F_j(U)\right)_{i=1}^M.$$
The collocation stages and endpoint are the implicit Runge–Kutta equations of [[def-implicit-runge-kutta-stage-equations]] with $A=Q$, nodes $c$, and weights $b$:
$$U=\mathbf1u+hQF(U),\qquad \Psi_h(t,u)=u+h\sum_{j=1}^M b_jF_j(U).$$
The associated collocation polynomial on normalized time $\tau\in[0,1]$ is
$$u_h(\tau):=u+h\int_0^\tau\sum_{j=1}^M\ell_j(s)F_j(U)\,ds.$$
Thus $u_h(c_i)=U_i$, $u_h'(c_i)=hF_i(U)$, and $u_h(1)=\Psi_h(t,u)$ whenever $U$ is an admissible solution. This definition alone asserts no branch existence or uniqueness.

For interpolation estimates define the **Lebesgue constant** of this fixed node set by
$$\Lambda_M:=\max_{0\le s\le1}\sum_{j=1}^M|\ell_j(s)|.$$
For a real matrix $A$, write $\|A\|_\infty:=\max_i\sum_j|a_{ij}|$. These constants depend on the nodes and on $M$; no uniform-in-$M$ bound is part of the definition.
lem-collocation-quadrature-matrix-well-d:
## Statement

For the distinct nodes and cardinal polynomials in [[def-collocation-quadrature-tableau]], every entry of $Q$, every component of $b$, and the Lebesgue constant $\Lambda_M$ is a finite real number.
alg-explicit-left-euler-sdc-sweep:
## Definition

Fix the nodes, matrices $Q,b$, and interpolant of [[def-collocation-quadrature-tableau]]. Let $c_0=0$, $\Delta c_j=c_j-c_{j-1}$, and let $F_j^k=f(t+c_jh,U_j^k)$ for the current stage vector $U^k$. The left-Euler node-subinterval preconditioner has fixed initial column $a_i=c_1$ and stage block
$$ (Q_\Delta)_{ij}=\begin{cases}\Delta c_{j+1},&j<i,\\0,&j\ge i.\end{cases} $$
It is strictly lower triangular. In augmented notation, set $\widehat Q=(0\mid Q)$ and $\widehat Q_\Delta=(a\mid Q_\Delta)$, where the initial derivative $F_0=f(t,u)$ is fixed through all sweeps. One sweep is
$$U^{k+1}=\mathbf1u+h\widehat Q_\Delta(F_0,F(U^{k+1}))+h(\widehat Q-\widehat Q_\Delta)(F_0,F(U^k)).$$
The fixed initial-column contributions cancel. Thus the exact operational stage update is the forward recursion
$$U_i^{k+1}=u+h\sum_{j<i}(Q_\Delta)_{ij}F_j^{k+1}+h\sum_{j=1}^M(Q_{ij}-(Q_\Delta)_{ij})F_j^k,\quad i=1,\ldots,M.$$
After a sweep compute its update residual $r_k=\|U^{k+1}-U^k\|_{\infty,2}$, where $\|V\|_{\infty,2}=\max_i\|V_i\|_2$. If the stage field is $L$-Lipschitz on a supplied closed invariant stage set and
$$ a:=hL\|Q_\Delta\|_\infty<1,\qquad q:=\frac{hL\|Q-Q_\Delta\|_\infty}{1-a}<1,$$
then the residual test $r_k\le(1-q)\,\mathrm{tol}$ returns $U^k$ with status `residual-tolerance-met`; the separate stage-error theorem establishes what this status certifies. The endpoint for an accepted stage vector is $u+h\sum_jb_jF_j^k$.

The inputs are $t,u,h>0$, the vector field and admissible stage domain, distinct ordered nodes, a constant initial predictor $U^0=\mathbf1u$ (or another declared predictor), a Lipschitz bound $L$, tolerance $\mathrm{tol}>0$, and an integer sweep budget $K\ge0$. Reject repeated or unordered nodes as `invalid-node-data`; reject a stage outside the IVP domain as `inadmissible-stage`; if the displayed contraction inequalities are not certified, return `contraction-not-certified`; if the tolerance is not reached in at most $K$ sweeps, return `iteration-budget-exhausted` and no accepted endpoint. These statuses never assert convergence.

With the constant predictor, setup forms $Q,b,Q_\Delta$ once. Evaluating $F(U^0)$ costs $M$ right-hand-side calls, each outer sweep costs $M$ new calls, and the old stage values $F(U^k)$ are stored and reused; $K$ sweeps therefore use $M(K+1)$ stage calls. Matrix setup stores $O(M^2)$ coefficients; each sweep uses $O(M^2d)$ scalar arithmetic in addition to its right-hand-side calls. The claims use exact real arithmetic and give no floating-point roundoff guarantee.
lem-sdc-fixed-point-is-collocation-stage:
## Statement

For an admissible stage vector $U$, the fixed-point equation for one sweep of [[alg-explicit-left-euler-sdc-sweep]] holds if and only if $U=\mathbf1u+hQF(U)$, the collocation stage equation of [[def-collocation-quadrature-tableau]].
lem-one-node-gauss-data-is-midpoint:
## Statement

Assume Countable Choice for the Lebesgue interval-measure formula. For Lebesgue measure on $[0,1]$, the one-node Gaussian quadrature rule has node $c_1=1/2$ and weight $b_1=1$. Its one-stage collocation tableau therefore has $Q_{11}=1/2$ and endpoint weight $b_1=1$.
lem-sdc-scalar-linear-iteration-matrix:
## Statement

For the scalar test equation $y'=\lambda y$ and $z=h\lambda$, let $U^*$ be a collocation stage vector and $U^k$ the SDC iterates using the explicit-left-Euler stage block $Q_\Delta$ from [[alg-explicit-left-euler-sdc-sweep]]. Then
$$E^{k+1}=B(z)E^k,\qquad B(z):=(I-zQ_\Delta)^{-1}z(Q-Q_\Delta),\qquad E^k:=U^k-U^*.$$
The inverse exists for every real $z$ because $Q_\Delta$ is strictly lower triangular. In the induced infinity norm from [[def-collocation-quadrature-tableau]], $\|E^k\|_{\infty,2}\le\|B(z)\|_\infty^k\|E^0\|_{\infty,2}$. This identity makes no convergence claim when the powers of $B(z)$ do not tend to zero; stability of the fully solved collocation step alone is not an SDC iteration guarantee.
thm-sdc-sweep-contraction-and-error-boun:
## Statement

Let $\mathcal C$ be a nonempty closed product ball of stage vectors in $(\mathbb R^d)^M$, with metric $\|U-V\|_{\infty,2}=\max_i\|U_i-V_i\|_2$. Assume the forward sweep map in [[alg-explicit-left-euler-sdc-sweep]] maps every required stage vector into $\mathcal C$, and the stage field $F(U)=(f(t+c_i h,U_i))_{i=1}^M$ is $L$-Lipschitz there. Put
$$a=hL\|Q_\Delta\|_\infty,\qquad q=\frac{hL\|Q-Q_\Delta\|_\infty}{1-a}.$$
If $a<1$ and $q<1$, then every sweep is uniquely defined in $\mathcal C$, the sweep map $S:U^k\mapsto U^{k+1}$ is a contraction with constant $q$, and its unique fixed point $U^*$ is the unique collocation stage vector in $\mathcal C$. For every $V\in\mathcal C$,
$$\|V-U^*\|_{\infty,2}\le\frac{\|S(V)-V\|_{\infty,2}}{1-q}.$$
For iterates $U^{k+1}=S(U^k)$, $\|U^k-U^*\|_{\infty,2}\le q^k\|U^0-U^*\|_{\infty,2}$. These are local stage-iteration claims; they assert no convergence when either contraction inequality fails.
lem-collocation-polynomial-scaled-deriva:
## Statement

Fix $M$ distinct nodes in $[0,1]$. Assume $f$ has bounded continuous derivatives through order $2M+1$ on a compact tube containing the exact trajectory and the locally unique collocation stages for all sufficiently small $h>0$. Let $u_h$ be the collocation polynomial from [[def-collocation-quadrature-tableau]], and set
$$g_h(\tau)=f(t+h\tau,u_h(\tau)),\qquad r_h(\tau)=u_h'(\tau)-h g_h(\tau).$$
For $1\le j\le M$, $\|u_h^{(j)}\|_\infty\le C_jh^j$; for $j>M$, $u_h^{(j)}=0$. For $0\le j\le2M$, $\|g_h^{(j)}\|_\infty\le C_jh^j$ (with $h^0=1$), and
$$\|r_h^{(j)}\|_\infty\le C_j h^{j+1}.$$
The constants depend on the fixed node set and its cardinal-basis derivative bounds; no uniformity in $M$ is asserted.
thm-collocation-local-defect-order-m:
## Statement

Let $M\ge1$, let $0\le c_1<\cdots<c_M\le1$ be fixed distinct nodes, and consider $y'=f(t,y)$ on a fixed compact convex tube. Assume $f$ is $C^M$ with bounded derivatives there, is $L$-Lipschitz in state, and the exact path, stages, collocation polynomial, and comparison segments stay in the tube. In particular, the interpolation hypothesis is that the composite $g_h(s)=f(t+hs,y(t+hs))$ satisfies $\|g_h^{(M)}\|_\infty\le C_Fh^M$ uniformly; the stated smoothness and bounded exact-path derivatives imply this bound. If the collocation stage branch is the unique branch supplied by [[thm-sdc-sweep-contraction-and-error-bound]], then its endpoint map has uniform exact-start local defect $O(h^{M+1})$ as $h\downarrow0$. The constant depends on the fixed nodes, including their Lebesgue constant $\Lambda_M$; no uniform-in-$M$ estimate is asserted.
thm-collocation-one-step-stability:
## Statement

Let $f$ be $L$-Lipschitz in state on a common invariant stage tube, and let the collocation stage branches for initial states $u,v$ lie in that tube. If $hL\|Q\|_\infty\le1/2$, then
$$\|U(u)-U(v)\|_{\infty,2}\le2\|u-v\|_2.$$
Consequently the collocation step map $\Psi_h(u)=u+h\sum_jb_j f(t+c_jh,U_j(u))$ satisfies
$$\|\Psi_h(u)-\Psi_h(v)\|_2\le(1+2hL\|b\|_1)\|u-v\|_2,\qquad \|b\|_1:=\sum_j|b_j|.$$
lem-gauss-collocation-weighted-defect-bo:
## Statement

Assume Countable Choice for the Lebesgue interval-measure formula. Fix $M\ge1$ and the $M$-node Gauss rule for Lebesgue measure on $[0,1]$. Let $u_h$ be its collocation polynomial for an exact-start IVP $y'=f(t,y)$, and put $g_h(s)=f(t+hs,u_h(s))$. Assume $f$ is $C^{2M+1}$ with all derivatives through that order bounded on a common compact convex tube containing the exact path, $u_h$, and every segment joining them; the collocation branch and tube are uniform for sufficiently small $h$. Use the induced Euclidean operator norm $\|A\|_{op}:=\sup_{\|v\|_2=1}\|Av\|_2$, and assume $\|D_yf\|_{op}\le L$ on the tube. Then its endpoint defect satisfies
$$\|y(t+h)-u_h(1)\|_2\le C h^{2M+1},$$
where $C$ may depend on the fixed nodes and on $M$.
prop-one-node-gauss-collocation-order-tw:
## Statement

Assume Countable Choice for the Lebesgue interval-measure formula. Let $f(t,y)$ be $C^2$ on a common compact convex tube and Lipschitz in $y$ there. Assume the small-step one-stage collocation branch exists uniquely in this tube and its stages, the exact path, and the segments used in the estimates remain there. For the one-node Gaussian tableau of [[lem-one-node-gauss-data-is-midpoint]], the method is the implicit midpoint rule and has global order two on any fixed interval for which these hypotheses hold uniformly.
thm-collocation-global-order-m:
## Statement

Let $M\ge1$ and suppose the hypotheses of [[thm-collocation-local-defect-order-m]] and [[thm-collocation-one-step-stability]] hold uniformly on a fixed interval $[0,T]$. Starting with the exact initial value and using the collocation endpoint map on a uniform mesh, the maximum grid error is $O(h^M)$ as $h=T/N\downarrow0$.
thm-sdc-finite-sweeps-raise-order:
## Statement

Fix $M\ge1$ collocation nodes and a nonnegative integer $k$ independent of $h$. Use the explicit-left-Euler SDC sweep in [[alg-explicit-left-euler-sdc-sweep]] with constant predictor $U^0=\mathbf1u$ and form the candidate endpoint from $U^k$, after $k$ completed sweeps. Assume $f$ is $C^M$, state-Lipschitz with constant $L$, and bounded by $B$ on a common tube containing the exact path, all iterates, and the comparison segments; assume the exact-path integrand has the derivative bound required by [[thm-collocation-local-defect-order-m]]. Assume the stage set is invariant for the $k$ sweeps for every initial state in each stated time fiber, and the contraction theorem holds uniformly with $a=hL\|Q_\Delta\|_\infty\le1/2$ and $q\le C_qh<1$. For fixed $k$, the $U^k$ endpoint map has exact-start defect $O(h^{p+1})$ and global order $p=\min(M,k+1)$ on any fixed interval, provided all grid states stay in the tube. The claim is local-step and fixed-$k$; it asserts no uniform constants as $M$ or $k$ grows.
thm-sdc-residual-tolerance-preserves-ord:
## Statement

Fix $M$ nodes and an integer $1\le p\le M$. On a fixed interval use exact collocation stages $U_n^*$ and the collocation endpoint map $\Psi_{h,n}$ of [[def-collocation-quadrature-tableau]]. Assume the hypotheses of [[thm-sdc-sweep-contraction-and-error-bound]] hold uniformly, with contraction constants $q_n\le q_0<1$, the common field Lipschitz constant is $L$, and all exact and approximate stages and grid states stay in one compact tube. Suppose the SDC stage vector $V_n$ used for the endpoint satisfies
$$\|S_n(V_n)-V_n\|_{\infty,2}\le(1-q_n)C_\tau h^{p+1}.$$
Starting from the exact initial value and setting $y_{n+1}=y_n+h\sum_jb_jf(t_n+c_jh,(V_n)_j)$, the inexact method has global error $O(h^p)$. Thus a fixed residual constant and a stage target $O(h^{p+1})$ preserve any collocation order $p\le M$; the bound is conditional on the stated local contraction and tube assumptions.
thm-gauss-collocation-local-defect-order:
## Statement

Assume Countable Choice for the Lebesgue interval-measure formula. Let $M\ge1$ and let $f(t,y)$ be $C^{2M+1}$ with bounded derivatives on a common compact convex tube along an exact IVP path, its collocation branch, and connecting segments. Use the $M$-node Gaussian rule for Lebesgue measure on $[0,1]$, assume $\|D_yf\|_{op}\le L$ there, and assume the stage branch is uniquely defined there for all sufficiently small $h$. Then the exact-start local defect of the collocation endpoint is $O(h^{2M+1})$ as $h\downarrow0$. Its constant depends on the fixed nodes and $M$.
thm-gauss-collocation-global-order-2m:
## Statement

Assume Countable Choice as required by [[thm-gauss-collocation-local-defect-order-2m]]. Let $M\ge1$ and suppose the hypotheses of that theorem and [[thm-collocation-one-step-stability]] hold uniformly on a fixed interval $[0,T]$. Starting with the exact initial value and using the $M$-node Gauss collocation endpoint map on a uniform mesh, the maximum grid error is $O(h^{2M})$ as $h=T/N\downarrow0$.
